entries.title: At least 27 killed in Bangkok bar fire
entries.snippet: Firefighters arrived at the scene in the Chatuchak district to find patrons running through flames to escape.

entries.title: US insists Strait of Hormuz is open as it exchanges strikes with Iran
entries.snippet: Iranian forces earlier said the Strait was closed and launched wide-ranging attacks at US allies and bases in the region.

entries.title: US senator and close Trump ally Lindsey Graham dies after 'brief and sudden illness'
entries.snippet: A spokesman for the 71-year-old South Carolina senator says initial findings suggest Graham's cause of death was related to his heart.

entries.title: Anthony Zurcher: From Trump critic to ally, Lindsey Graham was a political survivor of the Maga era
entries.snippet: The senator's career was marked by a willingness to adapt to America's dramatically changing political climate, writes the BBC's North America correspondent.

entries.title: US Senator Mitch McConnell says absence due to fall and pneumonia
entries.snippet: The veteran Republican says he will not return to work "quite yet", in his first statement following weeks of speculation about his health.

entries.title: Badly burned British couple rescued from ravine during Spain wildfires, reports say
entries.snippet: The unnamed pair were found semi-conscious with 40% burns after being trapped by the blazes raging through Almeria province, local media reports.

entries.title: China evacuates nearly two million people as powerful typhoon makes landfall
entries.snippet: Schools, work and outdoor activities have been suspended in Zhejiang province and many transport services cancelled.

entries.title: T. rex could become most expensive fossil ever - but it's a ​problem for scientists
entries.snippet: A 67 million-year-old Tyrannosaurus rex will go on sale in New York with a pre-sale value of $30m.

entries.title: Former Emir of Qatar Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies aged 74
entries.snippet: He took power in 1996 after staging a bloodless coup against his father, and went on to transform Qatar into the gas-rich power it is today.

entries.title: David Willey, esteemed BBC Vatican correspondent, dies aged 93
entries.snippet: One of the BBC's longest-serving foreign correspondents, he reported on five popes during his career.

entries.title: South Africa says more than 53,000 foreigners deported in migration campaign
entries.snippet: South Africa is cracking down on undocumented migrants following widespread anti-immigration protests.

entries.title: At least two killed in Toronto street festival shooting
entries.snippet: Police say there was an exchange of gunfire between two individuals at the festival, and two firearms had been recovered from the scene.

entries.title: Muslim judge in India faces death threats after convicting 'cow vigilantes'
entries.snippet: Tabassum Khan has been facing online abuse after convicting 14 Hindu men in a lynching case.

entries.title: Polish PM pledges memorial to victims of WW2 'genocide by Ukrainian nationalists'
entries.snippet: Warsaw and Kyiv have for decades been at loggerheads over the killings of many thousands of civilians during World War Two.

entries.title: US Democrat Ro Khanna says he was detained by armed Israeli settlers
entries.snippet: Khanna, 49, was visiting the occupied West Bank when he was held for 90 minutes, he says.

entries.title: Trump administration subpoenas New York Times journalists over Air Force One reporting
entries.snippet: The reporters received the legal summons after they reported on alleged security issues with the president's new plane, which was gifted by Qatar.

entries.title: South Africa World Cup midfielder Adams dies aged 25
entries.snippet: South Africa and Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder Jayden Adams dies at the age of 25, just weeks after featuring for his country at the World Cup.

entries.title: More than 40 kidnapped children and teachers freed after Nigerian army operation
entries.snippet: "I feel happy and elated… I feel joy," the head of the local teachers' union tells the BBC.

entries.title: Indian tourists among 15 killed as speedboat capsizes in Vietnam
entries.snippet: Local media say 21 people were saved after the boat overturned in rough seas near an island in south Vietnam.

entries.title: How Indian scientists are mapping the brain's last frontier
entries.snippet: India's new brainstem atlas offers scientists an unprecedented map of one of the brain's least known regions.

entries.title: Want to own a real T. rex? It could cost you $30 million
entries.snippet: The Tyrannosaurus rex fossil known as "Gus" will go up for auction on Tuesday. It's not the first time dinosaur bones have been sold to the highest bidder.

entries.title: Georgia's unique in the American Revolution told through its historical markers
entries.snippet: NPR's Don Gonyea speaks with Andrew Iden, Executive Producer of Marked!: The Podcast , which examines Georgia's role in America's revolutionary period through the 2,000 roadside historical marker.

entries.title: Fire breaks out at a pub in Bangkok, killing at least 27 people, officials say
entries.snippet: Footage shared online by first responders shows a huge blaze raging and plumes coming out of the front door of the pub in the northern part of the Thai capital.

entries.title: Toronto police looking for suspects after deadly shooting at festival
entries.snippet: At least two people are dead and at least four people are injured after a shooting on Saturday night at a festival celebrating Latin culture in Canada's biggest city.

entries.title: What to know about the cyclosporiasis outbreak hitting more than half of U.S. states
entries.snippet: A surge of cases of the intestinal illness that causes diarrhea and nausea has been detected in 31 states, according to federal health authorities, but the source is still under investigation.

entries.title: A Bible passage is at the center of a debate over how the U.S. should treat immigrants
entries.snippet: A debate over the Bible verse Matthew 25 is pitting mainline pastors, Black protestants and the pope against evangelical politicians put on the defensive over President Trump's policies.

entries.title: A promising tale from Senegal of fish, rice .... and dangerous worms
entries.snippet: Farmers in Senegal are welcoming fish into their rice paddies. The hope is they'll fertilize the crop, be a source of food ... and eat the snails that carry parasitic worms.

entries.title: Campaign text messages could soon get more effective — and annoying
entries.snippet: Taught to sound like a candidate, bots are engaging voters with personalized text messages, making AI-generated texting conversations the latest tool political campaigns are using to connect.

entries.title: What a Monopoly importer learned when it tried to make things in the U.S.A.
entries.snippet: After getting hit with tariffs for the imported board games he sells, Jonathan Silva decided to see if he could produce a version of his Monopoly game in the United States. This is what he learned.

entries.title: An artist brought 'I.C.E. pops' to a Texas campus. The show was shut down in days
entries.snippet: The Trump administration's executive orders have meant that administrators are questioning what art can — and can't — be seen on campus.

entries.title: What to know about new rules and technology behind the World Cup's most contentious calls
entries.snippet: The sending off of Switzerland's Breel Embolo in Saturday's quarterfinal game against Argentina was the latest call that may have left fans scratching their heads.

entries.title: Lindsey Graham remembered for a vision of American foreign policy that's fading in Washington
entries.snippet: Graham was a rare bridge between President Donald Trump's "America First" foreign policy and the traditional Washington consensus prioritizing alliances with Europe and Israel, one falling out of favor with many in both political parties.

entries.title: McConnell says a fall led to his hospitalization, breaking weeks of silence about health condition
entries.snippet: McConnell, 84, explained the long silence about his condition by saying that "folks of my generation often hesitate to share the vulnerability that comes with growing older."

entries.title: Innovation, data fixes fuel Native American graduation gains at federally funded schools
entries.snippet: In 2015, just over half of high schoolers at Bureau of Indian Education schools graduated within four years. That number soared to a record high of 79% by 2025.

entries.title: Syria's new parliament holds first session since ouster of ex-President Assad
entries.snippet: The launch of the parliament indicates Syria is moving ahead with drafting new laws as it recovers from decades of brutal rule under the Assad family and a deadly civil war that killed about half a million people.

entries.title: From staunch critic to fierce ally: Graham's long, strange and consequential friendship with Trump
entries.snippet: After the Capitol riot on Jan. 6, 2021, Sen. Lindsey Graham said he had finally had enough of the man who was championed by the mob that stormed the pillar of American democracy: President Donald Trump.

entries.title: When managing your money, take a chatbot's 'confidence' with a grain of salt
entries.snippet: According to a 2025 survey of 2,000 U.S. adults by Pearl.com, a professional services platform, 19% said they lost more than $100 by following financial advice from an AI chatbot.

entries.title: Keystone Pipeline system's operator agrees to pay $26.9M penalty over major Kansas oil spill
entries.snippet: The rupture in December 2022 dumped nearly 13,000 barrels of heavy crude oil into a creek running through a rural pasture in Washington County, Kansas, about 150 miles northwest of Kansas City.

entries.title: Georgia teen charged in Apalachee High School shooting to appear in court for plea and sentencing
entries.snippet: Colt Gray, 16, had pleaded not guilty to charges including murder in the shooting that killed two students and two teachers, and left several others wounded, at the high school northeast of Atlanta.

entries.title: Ukraine's prime minister steps down as Zelenskyy announces government reshuffle
entries.snippet: Zelenskyy, who has remained in office under martial law because wartime elections are prohibited, has periodically reshuffled his government in an effort to bring fresh momentum to his administration.

entries.title: U.S. launches more strikes on Iran as the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz escalates
entries.snippet: Iran's state-run IRNA news agency cited the governor of Qeshm island near the strait as saying projectiles had been fired at military targets, with no casualties.

entries.title: Lindsey Graham, longtime Republican senator, dies at 71 after 'brief and sudden illness'
entries.snippet: The statement his office posted on social media did not provide any additional details about the circumstances surrounding the Saturday night death of the South Carolina Republican, a former Air Force lawyer who served in Congress for three decades.

entries.title: Guggenheim Museum among NYC buildings that tested positive for Legionnaires' amid disease outbreak
entries.snippet: The city health department on Friday released a list of 31 buildings on the Upper East Side that have been ordered to clean and disinfect their cooling towers as the city deals with the latest outbreak of the disease.

entries.title: Sen. Whitehouse announces whistleblower allegations of construction problems at Kennedy Center
entries.snippet: Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island said in a release on Saturday that he had received a whistleblower disclosure from the Government Accountability Project.

entries.title: Judge tosses remnants of Proud Boys seditious conspiracy case after Trump's broad clemency
entries.snippet: The judge who presided over the Proud Boys leaders' trial saw no basis to preserve the convictions after Trump's sweeping act of clemency last year.

entries.title: Rep. Ro Khanna says he was detained by the Israeli military and settlers in the West Bank
entries.snippet: A representative for Khanna, a California Democrat who is an outspoken progressive, said the confrontation occurred Wednesday in the middle of a three-day tour of the West Bank.

entries.title: New York Times reporters are subpoenaed after Air Force One stories, raising press freedom concerns
entries.snippet: The subpoenas seek to force the reporters to testify before a federal grand jury in Manhattan next week, the Times said, adding that federal agents delivered some subpoenas to the reporters at their homes.

entries.title: Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in eastern China as more than 1 million are evacuated
entries.snippet: Bavi previously brought strong winds and rain to Japan's southern islands and Taiwan. It was the second typhoon to impact China in just over a week's time.

entries.title: UK police make new arrest over killing of former politician Ann Widdecombe
entries.snippet: Devon and Cornwall Police said the suspect was arrested more than 200 miles from the southwest England village where Widdecombe was found dead.

entries.title: Fate of Strait of Hormuz challenges talks as Trump and Iran's supreme leader trade threats
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump overnight made threats on social media of further missile attacks against Iran, after the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei saw open calls for the U.S. leader's killing.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Iran war: US carries out fresh strikes near Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: The US army said the strikes near the vital waterway were intended to "degrade" Tehran's ability to attack commercial ships. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Venezuela sets up temporary housing, as death toll rises to almost 4,500
entries.snippet: As the official death toll from the devastating earthquakes which struck northern Venezuela last month continues to rise, authorities are planning to set up temporary housing to shelter thousands of people left homeless.

entries.title: Sinner beats Zverev to retain Wimbledon title
entries.snippet: Jannik Sinner retained his Wimbledon title by beating Alexander Zverev in Sunday's men's final. The Italian claims his fifth Grand Slam crown and extends his dominance over the German to 10 straight victories.

entries.title: France opens terror probe after gun found in Jewish suburb
entries.snippet: Police said they found a "military-grade weapon" during the search of a suspicious car parked in a Paris neighborhood with a large Jewish population.

entries.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy swaps out prime minister in reshuffle
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president announced a government shake up, with PM Yuliia Svyrydenko stepping down after a year in office.

entries.title: Are German companies leaving the country?
entries.snippet: Should I stay or should I go? Given Germany's high cost and sluggish growth, some business leaders are mulling relocating, or at least investing abroad. DW has a look at the numbers.

entries.title: EU defense remains heavily reliant on the United States
entries.snippet: There are many obstacles as EU governments seek to reduce their dependence on the US. DW looks at the European Unions's attempts to develop counterparts to Patriot and Tomahawk missiles, F-35 jets, and Starlink internet.

entries.title: California’s largest lake is turning to dust
entries.snippet: The Salton Sea is drying up, worsening air pollution for people living near its shores. Authorities are working to stabilize the lakebed and lock down the dust. But for some families, it's too late.

entries.title: Germany's Ruhr Valley is on brink of financial collapse
entries.snippet: With tax revenues down and social spending up, more and more cities and towns in the Ruhrgebiet are struggling to make ends meet. One city that is particularly deep in the red is Oberhausen.

entries.title: Germany news: Neuschwanstein killer fights extradition to US
entries.snippet: A man who murdered a woman at Neuschwanstein Castle says he fears execution in the US. Germany has been hit by another heat wave, though no records are likely to be broken this time, forecasters say.

entries.title: Qatar: Former Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies at 74
entries.snippet: The former Emir led Qatar's transformation from a small Gulf state into one of the world's wealthiest nations and oversaw the launch of Al Jazeera and the country's World Cup bid.

entries.title: How a Jewish heir is taking on Germany's far-right AfD
entries.snippet: Heavily supported in eastern states, the Alternative for Germany is using a GDR cultural icon, the Schwalbe moped, in its campaigning. Now, the Jewish heir of the manufacturer is fighting to protect his family's legacy.

entries.title: Could AI help al-Qaeda and other groups plan terror attacks?
entries.snippet: Followers of extremist groups regularly ask how AI can help them plan terrorist attacks. A new study suggests that about one-third of AI chatbots might help them, if asked the right way.

entries.title: US: Reporters subpoenaed over Air Force One stories
entries.snippet: New York Times journalists who reported on security fears about the president's new Qatari-gifted plane have been called to court. The case raises concerns about press freedoms under the Trump administration.

entries.title: US Senator Lindsey Graham dies
entries.snippet: The South Carolina politician and staunch ally of Donald Trump died aged 71 after ​a brief and sudden illness, his office said. The hawkish senator backed the 2003 invasion of Iraq and the more recent war with Iran.

entries.title: Gas queues grow as Ukraine targets Russia's fuel supply
entries.snippet: Attacks by Ukraine have triggered a fuel crisis in Russia. Reports from across Russia show how residents are dealing with the disruptions in their daily lives.

entries.title: Two people killed and several wounded in mass shooting at Toronto festival
entries.snippet: The shooting happened during a salsa event, Canada's largest Latin street festival. Toronto police say two gunmen were responsible but that the suspects have not been detained yet.

entries.title: Iran war: US claims Strait of Hormuz is 'open' amid strikes
entries.snippet: US President Trump and the US military's Central Command insisted on Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz is open despite the Iranian navy declaring it closed. Both sides continue to exchange strikes.

entries.title: Spain wildfire: Firefighters begin to contain deadly blaze
entries.snippet: Firefighters have started to rein in the wildfire that killed 12 people in the southern Andalusia region, which is home to one of Spain's largest expat communities.
